provenance: Lane split authored by Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only; returns JSON in its reply) and persisted here by the orchestrator. technique_name/tactic reconciled against intel/cti-pipeline.json; rationale carries the Stage-1 detection_feasibility note.

detection_candidates.rationale: medium — attachment-based spearphishing is detectable via mail sandboxing and macro/XLL/.accdb content analysis at the gateway
medium — link-based spearphishing is detectable via URL rewriting/detonation and proxy telemetry, though geofencing degrades sandbox coverage
high — Office/Excel spawning script or child processes after macro/XLL enablement is a core detectable behavior
high — script-block/module logging and suspicious PowerShell parenting (Office->PowerShell) are well-covered detections

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
detection_candidates.rationale: high — cmd.exe execution with anomalous parents (Office, script hosts, backdoor processes) is visible in process-creation logs

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: high — wscript/cscript executing VBS, especially spawned by Office, is a strong detectable signal
medium — PyInstaller-packed binaries are detectable via unusual temp _MEI extraction folders and bundled-python process behavior rather than a python.exe command line
medium — wscript/mshta-hosted JS is detectable via script-host process lineage and script-block logging
high — WMI process creation and WMI-Activity operational logs provide strong telemetry
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational) and highly detectable, especially with script actions

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — Run-key writes and Startup-folder file drops are detectable via registry and file-creation telemetry
medium — injection is detectable via EDR memory/API telemetry (CreateRemoteThread, RWX allocations) but requires endpoint depth
high — msiexec.exe executing MSI packages from user-writable/temp paths or with network sources is a detectable LOLBin pattern

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: HTML Smuggling
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — HTML smuggling is detectable via JS blob/anchor-download inspection at the proxy and browser-download telemetry, but bypasses attachment scanning
medium — runtime decode routines are detectable via script-block logging and certutil/PowerShell decode command-lines where used
high — remote downloads and unexpected inbound file writes are strongly detectable in process + network telemetry
medium — HTTP C2 is detectable via proxy/beacon analytics and URI/JA3 anomalies but blends with normal web traffic
medium — exfil over the C2 channel is detectable via outbound-volume/beacon analytics on the same session, but blends with C2 traffic

detection_candidates.technique_name: Credentials from Password Stores: Credentials from Web Browsers
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — access to browser Login Data stores and known-tool execution are detectable via file-access and process signatures

hunting_candidates.rationale: medium — link clicks are visible in email/URL-gateway and proxy logs; endpoint signal is indirect until the archive is opened
medium — signed-malware is detectable via certificate-reputation/thumbprint hunting and signature-anomaly analytics on loaded binaries

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — packed binaries are common and packing alone is weakly indicative; hunt candidate via packer-signature/entropy analytics rather than a standalone alert
low — archive delivery is ubiquitous; better as gateway archive-inspection/hunt than a standalone endpoint detection

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion: User Activity Based Checks
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — pre-payload sandbox/user-activity checks leave little host log signal; hunt candidate via static analysis of the sample

hunting_candidates.technique_name: System Location Discovery: System Language Discovery
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — a single locale/keyboard-layout API query is near-invisible in host logs; hunt candidate via sample analysis, not endpoint detection
medium — systeminfo-style discovery is common; suspicious mainly in tight backdoor process-lineage context
medium — whoami/user-context queries are common; value is in process-lineage correlation with the backdoor
low — file/directory enumeration is high-volume and hard to isolate; behavioral hunt candidate
medium — AV-product enumeration (WMI SecurityCenter / registry / service queries) is detectable when tied to a backdoor's process lineage
medium — process enumeration is common but meaningful in backdoor process-lineage context
low — screen-capture APIs leave little discrete log signal; behavioral/EDR hunt candidate
medium — base64-encoded C2 content is detectable via network inspection and encoding heuristics where TLS is absent

low — cloud-service C2 rides trusted SaaS domains and TLS; not detectable by domain reputation alone. Hunt candidate via anomalous process-to-SaaS-API behavior (backdoor/PyInstaller process talking to Dropbox/Facebook APIs) and CASB/egress analytics
low — bidirectional SaaS-API C2 is indistinguishable from legitimate cloud use at the network layer; hunt candidate via endpoint process-behavior baselining and cloud-app API-token anomaly detection
low — exfil to trusted SaaS blends with sanctioned cloud use; hunt candidate via DLP/CASB upload-volume anomalies and unusual process-to-cloud API activity

hunting_candidates.technique_name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
hunting_candidates.rationale: low — uploads to Dropbox are trusted by default; hunt candidate via CASB/egress upload-size anomalies and non-browser processes calling cloud-storage APIs
